newsitem.title: CHINA: KA WAH SURGES, OTHER SMALL HK BANKS RISE.
newsitem.headline: KA WAH SURGES, OTHER SMALL HK BANKS RISE.

text.p: Small banking shares continued to surge on Thursday, led by a rally in Ka Wah Bank Ltd which said earlier it was considering a proposal to become a wholly owned subsidiary of a new holding company.
Ka Wah Bank shares were up HK$1.40 at HK$12.30, while Liu Chong Hing Bank Ltd gained HK$1.50 to HK$22.20 and Wing Hang Bank Ltd rose HK$1.00 to HK$47.60.
"I think people are becoming more sanguine about the competitive situation on mortgages," said Alan Hutcheson, banking analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
"There is still a reasonable amount of speculation on the China-related banks that some deals might happen in the sector."
Small banks also surged on Wednesday as investors hoped for better earnings following a recent rise in mortgage rates by major banks.
Stanley Ng, research manager at Mansion House Research, said the rise in Ka Wah Bank shares was driven by the bank's consideration of a proposal to become a unit of a new holding company.
The holding company, to be incorporated in Bermuda, would be listed on the stock exchange and Ka Wah shares would be delisted.
"The rise is mainly because of market talk that its parent company CITIC Beijing is ready to inject assets into the new holding company and expand the new company," said Ng.
Hutcheson said it would be easier for the holding company to buy assets since Ka Wah was restricted under the banking ordinance in the kinds of assets it could buy.
China International Trust and Investment Corp held 61.25 percent of Ka Wah Bank in late May.
